cohort: 63,334 pregnancies delivered between 2010 and 2017 in the University of Pennsylvania Health System
finding: Both individual-level risk factors (cesarean delivery, stillbirth, preeclampsia diagnosis, and race) and neighborhood-level risk factors (percentage of individuals in a Census tract who identified as Black or African American) were independently associated with severe maternal morbidity.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with higher odds of severe maternal morbidity (aOR 3.50, 95% CI 3.15-3.89).
